title: Acute Decompensated Heart Failure and Cardiogenic Shock

steps.tx: The **Universal Definition** of Heart Failure classifies patients based on ejection fraction into **HFrEF** with LVEF at most **40%**, **HFmrEF** with LVEF **41%** to **49%**, and **HFpEF** with LVEF at least **50%**. This standardized phenotypic stratification determines evidence-based medical therapy and identifies unique pathophysiological mechanisms.

steps.tx: The **Nohria-Stevenson** clinical classification categorizes acute decompensated heart failure into **4** hemodynamic profiles: Warm-Dry, **Warm-Wet**, Cold-Dry, and **Cold-Wet**. The Warm-Wet presentation represents well-perfused congestion, whereas the Cold-Wet profile reflects profound systemic hypoperfusion combined with elevated pulmonary capillary wedge pressure requiring urgent vasoactive support.

left.title: Warm-Wet Profile (Congested / Well-Perfused)
points: Accounts for > 70% of acute heart failure admissions
Elevated JVP, orthopnea, bilateral pulmonary crackles
Warm extremities with normal capillary refill time
Managed with IV loop diuretics and vasodilators

right.title: Cold-Wet Profile (Congested / Hypoperfused)
points: Severe cardiogenic decompensation and shock risk
Cool extremities, narrow pulse pressure, elevated lactate
Elevated filling pressures with low cardiac output
Requires inotropes, vasopressors, or mechanical support

steps.tx: B-type **natriuretic peptide** cutoff < **100** pg/mL and **NT-proBNP** cutoff < **300** pg/mL have a negative predictive value > **95%** for excluding acute decompensated heart failure in dyspneic emergency patients. Markedly elevated natriuretic peptides reflect ventricular wall stretch, guiding urgent clinical diagnosis.

steps.tx: Intravenous **loop diuretics** such as **furosemide** in acute decompensated heart failure are administered at **1** to **2.5** times the daily oral home dose to achieve effective decongestion as established in the DOSE trial. Early natriuretic assessment at two hours directs subsequent diuretic dose doubling in resistant states.
steps.say: Intravenous loop diuretics such as furosemide in acute decompensated heart failure are administered at 1 to 2 point 5 times the daily oral home dose to achieve effective decongestion as established in the DOSE trial. Early natriuretic assessment at two hours directs subsequent diuretic dose doubling in resistant states.

nodes.label: Acute Heart Failure Presentation with Volume Overload
Administer IV Furosemide at 1 to 2.5 Times Home Oral Dose
If Suboptimal: Double IV Diuretic Dose or Add Thiazide

steps.tx: Inotropic therapy in cardiogenic shock utilizes **dobutamine** which stimulates beta-**1** adrenergic receptors, or **milrinone** which inhibits phosphodiesterase-**3**, augmenting contractility at the expense of higher myocardial oxygen demand. Milrinone provides balanced peripheral vasodilation, proving advantageous in patients receiving chronic beta-blocker therapy. Comprehensive clinical evaluation requires careful correlation with serial electrocardiographic tracings and hemodynamic parameters.

left.title: Dobutamine Inotrope
points: Beta-1 and beta-2 adrenergic receptor agonist
Rapid onset and short 2-minute half-life
May provoke sinus tachycardia and ventricular ectopy
Hepatic clearance (safe in renal dysfunction)

right.title: Milrinone Inodilator
points: Phosphodiesterase-3 intracellular enzyme inhibitor
Bypasses down-regulated beta-adrenergic receptors
Reduces pulmonary vascular resistance and afterload
Eliminated by kidneys; requires dose adjustment in CKD

steps.tx: Intravenous vasodilators including **nitroglycerin** and sodium **nitroprusside** rapidly reduce preload and afterload in acute hypertensive pulmonary edema, lowering left ventricular filling pressures without compromising renal filtration. Nitroglycerin acts predominantly as a venodilator at low doses, while nitroprusside achieves balanced arterial and venous vasodilation.

left.title: Intravenous Nitroglycerin
points: Predominant venodilation reducing preload and PCWP
Coronary vasodilation relieves myocardial ischemia
Rapid titration with short duration of action
Tachyphylaxis develops with infusions exceeding 24-48 hours

right.title: Sodium Nitroprusside
points: Equipotent arterial and venous vasodilation
Dramatically reduces afterload in severe hypertension
Light-sensitive; risk of thiocyanate and cyanide toxicity
Requires continuous arterial line blood pressure monitoring

steps.tx: **Cardiorenal syndrome** type **1** describes acute kidney injury resulting directly from acute cardiac decompensation, driven predominantly by renal **venous congestion** and high central venous pressure rather than reduced forward arterial output. Elevated renal venous pressure compresses intrarenal parenchymal vessels, impeding glomerular filtration.

steps.tx: **Levosimendan** is a calcium-sensitizing inodilator that enhances cardiac myofilament **calcium sensitization** through binding troponin C and opens vascular ATP-sensitive potassium channels, producing inotropy and vasodilation without increasing myocardial oxygen consumption or intracellular calcium overload. It represents a non-arrhythmogenic inotropic alternative in decompensated states.
